body.en: Unit 2 treats exponential and logarithmic functions as models of multiplicative change — quantities that change by a constant factor over equal intervals, rather than a constant additive amount.

Domain: all reals. Range: \((0,\infty)\) when \(a>0.\) Horizontal asymptote: \(y=0.\)

Key property: Over any equal-length interval \(\Delta x\), the output is multiplied by the same factor \(b^{\Delta x}.\)

Growth: \(b>1.\) Decay: \(0<b<1.\) Natural base: \(e\approx2.71828.\)

\[f(x)=ae^{kx}:\quad k>0\Rightarrow\text{growth},\quad k<0\Rightarrow\text{decay}.\]

ariaLabel.en: An exponential curve P of t equals P naught e to the r t, changing shape as the continuous rate r varies between decay and growth

note.en: \(P(t)=P_0e^{rt}\) — the continuous-compounding form from Worked Example 2.3's car-depreciation model.

body.en:
\[\log_b(MN)=\log_b M+\log_b N,\quad\log_b\!\left(\frac{M}{N}\right)=\log_b M-\log_b N,\]\[\log_b(M^p)=p\log_b M,\quad\log_b x=\frac{\ln x}{\ln b}\quad(\text{change of base}).\]

Inverse relationship: \(b^{\log_b x}=x\) and \(\log_b(b^x)=x.\)

Key values: \(\log_b 1=0,\;\log_b b=1.\)

Exponential: isolate the exponential, apply \(\ln\) or \(\log\) to both sides.

Logarithmic: combine logs using properties, convert to exponential form.

Extraneous solutions: always check that arguments of logs are positive in the original equation.

problem.en: A bacteria culture starts with 400 and triples every 6 hours. Write \(P(t)\) and find when it reaches 10 800.
The value of a car is modelled by \(V(t)=25000\,e^{-0.12t}.\) (a) Find the initial value. (b) After how many years is the car worth $10,000? (c) What is the continuous rate of decay?

solution.en:
(a) \(V(0)=25000\,e^0=\$25{,}000.\)

(b) \(25000\,e^{-0.12t}=10000\Rightarrow e^{-0.12t}=0.4\Rightarrow -0.12t=\ln 0.4\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\ln 0.4}{-0.12}\approx7.6\) years.

(c) The continuous decay rate is \(|-0.12|=12\%\) per year.

caption.en: The graphs of \( f(x) = 2^x \) and its inverse \( g(x) = \log_2(x) \) are reflections across the line \( y = x \). The horizontal asymptote \( y = 0 \) of \( f(x) \) reflects into the vertical asymptote \( x = 0 \) of \( g(x) \), and the point \( (a, b) \) on \( f \) reflects to \( (b, a) \) on \( g \).

label.en: ▲ AP Exam Traps & Pitfalls — Exponential & Logarithmic Functions

body.en:
• Additive vs. Multiplicative Rates: Linear models have constant first differences; exponential models have constant ratios (proportional growth) over equal intervals. If outputs double when inputs increase by 3, the model is exponential with growth factor \(2^{1/3}\) per unit.
  • Logarithm Domain & Extraneous Solutions: In any logarithmic equation, the argument of every logarithm must be strictly positive: \(\log_b(g(x))\) requires \(g(x) > 0\). Potential solutions that make any original argument \(\le 0\) are extraneous and must be discarded.
  • Semi-Log vs. Log-Log Linearization: On the AP exam, data that fits an exponential model \(y = ab^x\) is linearized by plotting \(\ln(y)\) vs. \(x\) (semi-log plot: \(\ln y = \ln a + (\ln b)x\)). Data that fits a power model \(y = ax^b\) is linearized by plotting \(\ln(y)\) vs. \(\ln(x)\) (log-log plot: \(\ln y = \ln a + b\ln x\)).
  • Continuous Rate vs. Effective Growth Rate: In \(P(t) = P_0 e^{rt}\), \(r\) is the continuous growth rate. The effective 1-unit growth factor is \(b = e^r\), meaning the percentage increase per unit time is \((e^r - 1) \times 100\%\), which is slightly greater than \(r \times 100\%\) for growth.

question.en: Carbon-14 decays exponentially with a half-life of 5,730 years. A preserved artifact is discovered to contain 28% of its original \({}^{14}\text{C}\) content. (a) Write an exponential decay model \(A(t) = A_0 e^{kt}\) for the remaining proportion of carbon-14 after \(t\) years. (b) Determine the age of the artifact to the nearest 10 years.

solution.en:
(a) Continuous decay constant \(k\): At the half-life \(t = 5730\), \(A(5730) = 0.5 A_0\). Thus \(e^{5730k} = 0.5 \Rightarrow 5730k = \ln(0.5) \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{\ln(0.5)}{5730} \approx -0.00012097\text{ yr}^{-1}\). The model is \(A(t) = A_0 e^{-0.000121 t}\) (or \(A(t) = A_0 (0.5)^{t/5730}\)).

(b) Age calculation: Set \(A(t) = 0.28 A_0\): \((0.5)^{t/5730} = 0.28 \Rightarrow \dfrac{t}{5730} \ln(0.5) = \ln(0.28) \Rightarrow t = 5730 \cdot \dfrac{\ln(0.28)}{\ln(0.5)} \approx 5730 \cdot \dfrac{-1.272966}{-0.693147} \approx 10{,}520\) years. The artifact is approximately 10,520 years old.

question.en: A researcher collects experimental data and performs a semi-log regression, finding the linear relationship \(\ln(y) = -0.35x + 2.80\). (a) Express \(y\) explicitly as an exponential function of the form \(y = a \cdot b^x\). (b) Identify the initial value \(y(0)\) and the 1-unit decay factor \(b\). (c) Calculate \(y\) when \(x = 4\), rounding to 3 decimal places.

solution.en:
(a) Exponential form: Exponentiate both sides: \(y = e^{\ln(y)} = e^{-0.35x + 2.80} = e^{2.80} \cdot e^{-0.35x} = e^{2.80} \cdot (e^{-0.35})^x\). Since \(e^{2.80} \approx 16.4446\) and \(e^{-0.35} \approx 0.70469\), we have \(y = 16.445 \cdot (0.7047)^x\).

(b) Parameters: The initial value is \(a = e^{2.80} \approx 16.445\). The decay factor per unit increase in \(x\) is \(b = e^{-0.35} \approx 0.705\), representing an effective decay of approximately \(29.5\%\) per unit.

(c) Evaluation at \(x = 4\): \(\ln(y) = -0.35(4) + 2.80 = -1.40 + 2.80 = 1.40\). Thus \(y = e^{1.40} \approx 4.055\).
